title: Teaser or trailer
summary: A teaser or trailer of 6-60 s that builds anticipation for something not yet out or revealed: a coming-soon product, an event or conference, a course or channel, a countdown; ends on a title card with the date and where.

notFor.when: the product is out (or is being shown in full now) and the film sells it with its mechanism and proof
the film looks back on an event that already happened: an aftermovie or recap
a mood or brand montage of stock or supplied footage with no reveal or date
a feature or update that ships now, announced to existing users
an animated piece with nothing to reveal or announce: a logo ident, kinetic type, a title sequence
the film teaches the course's subject itself rather than selling the course

alternatives.when: real event, venue, speaker or course footage carries the film (last year's conference, recorded lessons)
an essential mystery shot no library block, capture or Blender scene can make, and the user has authorised a budget

route.start: pnpm film:init --project <id> --type motion-graphics --secondary ai-video --playbook teaser-trailer --profile promo --product <path>

qa: The title card's date, time zone and where (URL, store, venue, handle) match the intake answer character for character and read with sound off for at least their reading time
Nothing withheld is replaced by a stand-in: every partial shot is a crop, detail, silhouette or blur of the real product, venue or footage
The build shortens shot by shot into the drop, the drop is followed by a planned rest or silence in a quiet bar of the audio map, and the title card lands on a downbeat or the cue's final hit
Bursts (light-burn, flare-pulse, ground swaps) keep to at most three flashes in any one second: film:measure's flash-risk leg passes
The button after the title, if any, is under 3 s and never pushes the date card off the final frame

intake.ask: What is revealed, when (date, time zone) and where to go (URL, store, venue, handle, register link)?
intake.why: The date and where are the film's whole call to action; an invented or approximate date is a false claim.

intake.ask: How much may be shown before the reveal: everything, parts only (details, crops, silhouette), or nothing but the name?
intake.why: Withholding is the craft; it sets which shots exist and whether the product appears at all.
intake.default: Parts only: details and crops of the real thing, the whole only on or after the title card

intake.ask: What real material exists: product files, renders or a build; past event or venue footage; speaker photos; course recordings?
intake.why: Decides the film type (motion-graphics or footage) and rules out stand-ins.
intake.default: Only the logo and copy: motion-graphics with type, the real mark and abstract grounds

intake.ask: Where does it run and at what length: a 6 s bumper, a 15-34 s social cut, a 60 s site or channel trailer?
intake.why: A teaser and a trailer differ in structure (two acts or three), not only in length.
intake.default: One vertical 20-30 s cut for Reels, Shorts and TikTok

intake.ask: Does someone speak (a host, a speaker's line, a voiceover), or is it music, sound and type only?
intake.why: A voice adds captions and a dialogue mix; most teasers have none.
intake.default: No voice: music, sound design and type

intake.ask: One film, or a countdown series (for example T-7, T-3, T-1, today)?
intake.why: A series shares one system and reveals a little more each part.

profiles.note: Reels ads must be under 90 s at 9:16; keep the date, CTA and logo out of the bottom 35%.
In-feed allows up to 60 s and 21-34 s performs best; the hook in the first 3 s, no long logo intro, text inside the safe zones.
A vertical or square video up to 3 min is a Short; this task stays under 60 s.
Bumper ad: non-skippable, 5-6 s. One mystery shot, one hit, the title and date.
Channel or course trailer: shown only to non-subscribers, once; show, don't tell; shorter is better (band: house rule, starting point); one subscribe or enrol action.
LinkedIn recommends 15-30 s video ads and subtitles; an event or conference trailer for professionals.

starter.note: Mystery (decode, a slow focus pull on a detail), escalation (snap-zoom, ground swaps), the drop (light-burn), title and date (hero word, odometer for a countdown, end card). keynote-dark lights the product locally and keeps the rest unseen.

variants.title: Coming-soon product teaser
variants.changes: Two acts: mystery shots of real details, then one set piece and the title with the date. The product is never shown whole before the title; truth claims stay as unrevealed facts the user approves.

variants.title: Event or conference trailer
variants.changes: Three acts with footage when it exists (--type footage): place, people, then the headline speakers or acts as name cards; the end card carries dates, city, venue and the registration link.

variants.title: Course or channel trailer
variants.changes: Shows what the viewer gets, in real lessons or videos, with the host's voice when there is one (clean-sentence captions); ends on subscribe or enrol and where; up to 60 s landscape for the channel page.

variants.title: Countdown
variants.changes: A series on one system: the same grid, type and sound, the number on type-odometer-stat or type-hero-word, each part revealing one more detail; every part ends on the same date card.
